text:
sam.h: Heads-up: I'm proposing we change exporter defaults for the telemetry pipeline. Main idea: span-proxy should do protocol hedging (grpc -> http) + per-tenant retry budgets and a short request deadline. Wanted feedback before I open a PR.
anya: +1 on per-tenant budgets. we've seen noisy tenants cause long tail for everyone. what deadline are you thinking?
sam.h: thinking 6s default for user spans, 15s for bulk/ingest jobs. hedging delay 80ms (fire grpc, if no HEADERS in 80ms, start http attempt). keeps p99 latency down.
ben: hedging is attractive but we need to be careful with non-idempotent exporters. Are we assuming exporter requests are idempotent?
sam.h: good point. plan: require an idempotency header for hedged requests. collector will accept duplicate spans by default (we dedupe by idempotency-key + span id). fallback to single attempt if header missing.
kevin: can you sketch the config? I want to see how it fits with existing otel-collector config and our env vars.
sam.h: yep, rough YAML below:
```yaml
telemetry_exporter:
  protocol_fallback: true
  fallback_order: [grpc, http]
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    hedging_delay_ms: 80
    max_hedged_attempts: 2
  deadlines:
    default_ms: 6000
    ingest_ms: 15000
  retries:
    enabled: true
    max_retries: 3
    backoff:
      base_ms: 50
      factor: 2.0
      jitter: full # randomized +/- 100% to avoid thundering
  retry_budget:
    enabled: true
    tokens_per_minute: 1200
    per_tenant: true
  idempotency:
    header: X-Idempotency-Key
    enforce_for_hedging: true
```
anya: looks reasonable. For the retry_budget, how do you intend to surface metrics? we need per-tenant exhausted counters and a global throttled counter.
sam.h: exporter side will emit metrics: `exporter.retries.allowed`, `exporter.retries.used`, `exporter.retries.throttled`, and `exporter.hedged_attempts`. tag by tenant_id and route.
ben: what about gRPC deadlines vs HTTP timeouts? gRPC has a builtin deadline header; for HTTP we'll set `timeout` or `context` in the request. Need to ensure both respect the `default_ms` and don't double-count when hedging.
kevin: implementation detail: when hedging, both attempts still share the same logical deadline. So deadline starts at request receive, each attempt has per-attempt deadline = remaining_deadline - safety_slack (e.g., 40ms). Otherwise we risk both attempts running full duration.
anya: how does this interact with batching? Our span-batcher holds spans for N ms to batch. If hedging fires, we might send same batch twice. dedupe on ingest side must tolerate this.
sam.h: yes batch id + idempotency-key per batch. collector dedupes. we'll add a metric for deduped_count.
ben: failure modes: if upstream returns 503 with Retry-After, we should honor that and pause per-tenant token refills. Also circuit-breaker per upstream host/tenant would help.
kevin: agreed. add `circuit_breaker` config: sliding window, threshold, cooldown. Also add `respect_retry_after: true`.
sam.h: added to the PR plan. thoughts on backoff algorithm? currently we use linear backoff, but exponential + capped jitter seems better for correlated failures.
anya: exponential + full jitter is industry standard. cap at 2s/attempt to avoid long tails.
ben: curious about observability: we should expose trace of exporter attempts (span exported -> attach event for each attempt with status and which protocol used). we can then surface per-route SLOs in the console.
kevin: also add a config flag `emit_attempt_spans: bool` default false (high cardinality), can be turned on for debugging/canaries.
sam.h: +1. for rollout, plan is: 1) enable new defaults in telemetry-stage, 2) run canary with `emit_attempt_spans` for 24h, 3) monitor `exporter.retries.throttled` and dedupe rate, 4) slow rollout to prod.
anya: timeline?
sam.h: PR today, canary tomorrow, prod rollout next week if no regressions.
ben: small ask: document behaviour when protocol_fallback=false. i.e., only use configured protocol and don't hedging-start. keeps retro compatibility.
sam.h: good catch, will include explicit note in config docs and a migration note for any customers who rely on exact request counts.
ingest-bot: deployment scheduled: telemetry-stage/telemetry-exporter:v2-canary at 2025-11-05T09:00Z (auto).
kevin: thanks, I'll watch the dashboard and add a per-tenant alert for `exporter.retries.throttled > 0.05%` of requests over 10m.
anya: also add a dashboard chart: hedged_attempts / total_attempts and deduped_count.
sam.h: awesome. I'll open the PR and add the YAML + migration doc. Thanks for the fast feedback :thumbsup:
ben: :thumbsup:
kevin: :ok_hand:
